prompt.adult: Ephesians 2:9 says salvation is not of works. So that no one can do what?
prompt.child: Ephesians 2:9 says we are not saved by our works. That way, no one can do what?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 2:9 says salvation doesn't come from our works. Why? So that no one can what?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 2:9, salvation is not of works, lest anyone should do what?

verses.text: not of works, lest anyone should boast.

explanation.adult: Ephesians 2:9 gives the reason at the end. Read the last word.
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 2:9. The last word tells what no one can do.
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 2:9. The final word answers the question.
explanation.older: Ephesians 2:9 states the reason in its final word.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 2:8 says salvation is a gift of God. Ephesians 2:9 adds that it is not earned, and tells what that keeps anyone from doing.
teaching.takeaway: Salvation is not of works, lest anyone should boast.

prompt.adult: Ephesians 2:10 says we are His what, made for good works?
prompt.child: Ephesians 2:10 says God made us to do good works. It says we are His what?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 2:10 says God made us for good works. We are His what?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 2:10, what are believers called, created for good works?

verses.text: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.

explanation.adult: Ephesians 2:10 begins by saying what we are. Read the first words.
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 2:10. The first words tell what we are.
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 2:10. The answer is at the beginning.
explanation.older: Ephesians 2:10 states in its opening words what we are.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 2:10 says God made us and prepared good works for us to walk in. The first words say what we are to Him.
teaching.takeaway: We are His workmanship, created for good works.

prompt.adult: Ephesians 4:32 says to be kind and tenderhearted to one another. What other word describes how we are to treat one another?
prompt.child: Ephesians 4:32 tells us to be kind and tenderhearted. What else should we be toward each other?
prompt.teen: Besides kind and tenderhearted, how does Ephesians 4:32 say we should treat each other?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 4:32, along with being kind and tenderhearted, how are we to treat one another?

verses.text: And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ forgave you.

explanation.adult: Ephesians 4:32 lists three ways to treat each other. Read the third one.
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 4:32. It lists three things. Find the third.
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 4:32. Look at the third thing listed.
explanation.older: Ephesians 4:32 lists three qualities; the third is the answer, with the reason given after it.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 4:31 says to put away bitterness and anger. Ephesians 4:32 tells what to do instead, and it points to what God in Christ has done for us.
teaching.takeaway: We are to be kind, tenderhearted, and forgiving to one another.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: restored full Ephesians 4:32 (“Christ” is no longer another answer in this badge).

prompt.adult: What does Ephesians 6:1 tell children to do with their parents?
prompt.child: Ephesians 6:1 has a message for kids. What does it tell children to do with their parents?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 6:1 speaks to children. What does it tell them to do with their parents?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 6:1, what are children told to do regarding their parents?

verses.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.

explanation.adult: Ephesians 6:1 begins by speaking to children. Read the word right after "Children."
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 6:1. Look at the word right after "Children."
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 6:1. The instruction comes right after "Children."
explanation.older: Ephesians 6:1 gives the instruction directly after addressing children.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 6:1 gives children an instruction about their parents and says it is right. Read the first part of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Children are to obey their parents in the Lord.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: answer “Obey them” for parallel form with the other choices.

prompt.adult: Ephesians 6:2-3 says to honor your father and mother. What result does it promise?
prompt.child: Ephesians 6:2-3 says to honor your father and mother, and it gives a promise. What is promised?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 6:2-3 says to honor your father and mother. What good result does it promise?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 6:2-3, what is promised to those who honor their father and mother?

choices.text: A long life on the earth

verses.text: “Honor your father and mother,” which is the first commandment with promise:
“that it may be well with you and you may live long on the earth.”

explanation.adult: Ephesians 6:3 gives the promise. Read the end of that verse.
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 6:3. The end tells what is promised.
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 6:3. The promise is at the end.
explanation.older: Ephesians 6:3 states the promise, especially in its closing words.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 6:2 says this is the first commandment with a promise. Ephesians 6:3 tells what the promise is.
teaching.takeaway: Honoring father and mother comes with the promise of living long on the earth.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: trimmed padded wrongs so this correct answer is one of two longest in the badge.

prompt.adult: In the armor of God, what does Ephesians 6:17 say the sword of the Spirit is?
prompt.child: Ephesians 6:17 talks about the sword of the Spirit. What does it say the sword is?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 6:17 names the sword of the Spirit. What is that sword?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 6:17, what is the sword of the Spirit?

verses.text: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;

explanation.adult: Ephesians 6:17 explains what the sword is. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Ephesians 6:17. The end tells what the sword of the Spirit is.
explanation.teen: Check Ephesians 6:17. The last part says what the sword is.
explanation.older: Ephesians 6:17 identifies the sword of the Spirit in its final words.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ephesians 6:11-17 describes the whole armor of God piece by piece. The sword is the last piece, and the verse says what it really is.
teaching.takeaway: The sword of the Spirit is the word of God.

prompt.adult: Philippians 4:6 says not to be anxious about anything. How are we to make our requests known to God?
prompt.child: Philippians 4:6 says don't worry about anything. How should we tell God what we need?
prompt.teen: Philippians 4:6 says don't be anxious about anything. How should we bring our requests to God?
prompt.older: According to Philippians 4:6, by what are we to make our requests known to God instead of being anxious?

verses.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God;

explanation.adult: Philippians 4:6 tells how to bring requests to God. Read the words after "in everything."
explanation.child: Read Philippians 4:6. Look right after "in everything."
explanation.teen: Check Philippians 4:6. The answer comes right after "in everything."
explanation.older: Philippians 4:6 gives the means directly after "in everything."

teaching.extended_explanation: Philippians 4:6 gives something to do in place of worrying. Philippians 4:7 then says the peace of God will guard our hearts and minds.
teaching.takeaway: Instead of being anxious, we make our requests known to God by prayer.

prompt.adult: I can do ___ through Christ who strengthens me.
prompt.child: This verse says, “I can do ___ through Christ who strengthens me.” What goes in the blank?
prompt.teen: Complete the verse: I can do ___ through Christ who strengthens me.
prompt.older: According to Philippians 4:13, I can do ___ through Christ who strengthens me.

verses.text: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

explanation.adult: Philippians 4:13 says what the writer can do. Read the words right after “I can do.”
explanation.child: Read the first words of Philippians 4:13, right after “I can do.”
explanation.teen: Philippians 4:13 opens with what the writer can do. Look at the words that fill the blank.
explanation.older: Read the beginning of Philippians 4:13 for what goes after “I can do.”

teaching.extended_explanation: In Philippians 4:11-12, the writer says he learned to be content with much or with little. Philippians 4:13 tells what he can do, and through whom.
teaching.takeaway: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
